summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: discrete mathematics (sets, permutations, modular arithmetic, gcd and the Chinese remainder theorem, induction, binomial coefficients), the algorithms course (asymptotic notation, recurrences, Karatsuba, the FFT and FFT-based polynomial multiplication, bit-reversal, binary counters, stacks), introductory computability (Turing machines with multiple tapes and constant-factor simulations), and the supporting mathematics of a CS degree: calculus with limits, exponentials and Newton's method, complex numbers, and a first linear algebra course (matrices, rank, invertibility, subspaces, dimension, dot products and orthogonality over the reals, Gaussian elimination). They have not studied bilinear forms over general fields, tensor products of operators, Bruhat factorizations, algebraic complexity of integer multiplication beyond Karatsuba and the basic FFT, or research-level fast multiplication (Schönhage–Strassen, Fürer, Harvey–van der Hoeven, Nussbaumer transforms, Gaussian resampling), nor index coding or the Frankl–Wilson construction.

known.name: Asymptotic notation beyond big-O
known.gloss: Ω, Θ and o give asymptotic lower bounds, tight bounds and strictly smaller growth of functions, alongside big-O upper bounds.

known.name: Logarithms and exponents
known.gloss: The logarithm log_b x is the exponent to which b must be raised to get x; lg n here denotes the base-two logarithm rounded up.

known.name: Floor and ceiling
known.gloss: ⌊x⌋ is the largest integer at most x and ⌈x⌉ the smallest integer at least x.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a sum of digits times powers of a radix such as 2, with the leftmost digit most significant.

known.name: Schoolbook integer arithmetic with carries
known.gloss: Adding and multiplying integers digit by digit, passing carries to higher positions, which multiplies n-bit numbers in O(n²) bit operations.

known.name: Two's complement and signed integers
known.gloss: Standard ways of representing negative integers in binary, so that addition, subtraction and sign changes are simple bit operations.

known.name: XOR and arithmetic modulo 2
known.gloss: The bit operation that is 1 exactly when its two inputs differ, which is addition of bits modulo 2.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers where numbers are identified when their difference is divisible by a fixed modulus, so sums and products wrap around.

known.name: Prime numbers and gcd
known.gloss: A prime has no divisors other than 1 and itself; the gcd is the largest integer dividing two given integers, which are coprime when it is 1.

known.name: Euclidean algorithm
known.gloss: Repeated division with remainder that computes gcd(a,b) and, in its extended form, integers x,y with ax+by=gcd(a,b), giving inverses modulo b.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
known.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli, a system of congruences has a unique solution modulo their product, so Z/(n₁n₂)Z corresponds to pairs of residues.

known.name: Binomial coefficients and subsets
known.gloss: C(n,k) counts the k-element subsets of an n-element set; subsets are combined with intersection, union and Cartesian product.

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: A bijection from a finite set to itself, describing a reordering of items; permutations compose and have inverses.

known.name: Lexicographic order
known.gloss: Ordering tuples by their first coordinate, then by the second among ties, and so on, as for row-major storage of arrays.

known.name: Vectors and matrices
known.gloss: Rectangular arrays of numbers representing linear maps, multiplied by the row-times-column rule, with special forms such as identity, diagonal, permutation and triangular matrices.

known.name: Linear maps and invertibility
known.gloss: A map preserving sums and scalar multiples, given by a matrix; it is invertible when another linear map undoes it.

known.name: Vector spaces, subspaces and dimension
known.gloss: A set of vectors closed under linear combinations, with a dimension equal to the size of any basis; a subspace is such a set inside a larger one.

known.name: Rank of a matrix
known.gloss: The dimension of the space spanned by a matrix's columns, equal to that of its rows.

known.name: Dot product and orthogonality
known.gloss: The sum of coordinatewise products of two vectors; vectors are orthogonal when it is zero.

known.name: Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: Reducing a matrix by row operations to triangular or echelon form, used to solve linear systems and compute rank.

known.name: Fields and rings
known.gloss: Number systems with addition and multiplication obeying the usual laws; a field also has division by nonzero elements, as in Q, C or the integers modulo a prime.

known.name: Fast Fourier transform
known.gloss: The divide-and-conquer algorithm computing a length-n discrete Fourier transform in O(n log n) arithmetic operations by recursively combining half-length transforms with two-point butterflies.

known.name: Polynomial multiplication via evaluation and interpolation
known.gloss: Multiplying polynomials by evaluating them at roots of unity, multiplying values pointwise, and interpolating back, which the FFT makes O(n log n).

known.name: Bit-reversal permutation
known.gloss: The reordering of indices 0..2^k−1 that reverses the k-bit binary representation of each index, arising in in-place radix-two FFTs.

known.name: Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: Multiplying two n-digit numbers with three half-size products instead of four, giving O(n^{log₂3}) time.

known.name: Divide-and-conquer recurrences
known.gloss: Equations expressing an algorithm's cost on a problem through its cost on smaller subproblems, solved by unrolling or the master theorem.

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: Proving a statement for all natural numbers by proving a base case and that each case implies the next.

known.name: Geometric series
known.gloss: The sum a + ar + ar² + … , equal to a(1−r^k)/(1−r), bounded by a constant times its largest term when r is fixed away from 1.

known.name: Limits
known.gloss: The value a sequence approaches as its index grows; the limit inferior is the smallest value it keeps returning near.

known.name: Exponential function and Gaussians
known.gloss: The function e^x and its complex extension e^{iθ}=cosθ+i sinθ, including bell-shaped Gaussian functions e^{−cx²}.

known.name: Absolute value and the triangle inequality
known.gloss: The size |z| of a real or complex number, which satisfies |a+b| ≤ |a|+|b| and is used to bound accumulated errors.

known.name: Rounding to the nearest integer
known.gloss: Replacing a real number by the closest integer, which recovers an integer exactly when the approximation error is below 1/2.

known.name: Newton's method
known.gloss: An iteration x ↦ x − f(x)/f′(x) that roughly doubles the number of correct digits per step near a simple root, used for reciprocals and square roots.

known.name: Integer division and square root
known.gloss: For a,b>0, the unique q,r with a=bq+r and 0≤r<b, and the largest integer whose square is at most a.

known.name: Deterministic algorithm and worst-case running time
known.gloss: An algorithm whose steps are fixed by its input, measured by the maximum number of steps it takes over all inputs of a given length.

known.name: Stacks
known.gloss: A last-in first-out store; popping returns items in the reverse of the order they were pushed.

known.name: Binary counter
known.gloss: A register holding a number in binary that is incremented by flipping trailing ones and a zero, costing O(1) amortized bit flips per increment.

known.name: Hamming weight
known.gloss: The number of nonzero entries in a binary vector.

known.name: Matrix transposition
known.gloss: Rearranging an array so the entry at row i, column j moves to row j, column i.

known.name: Turing machine alphabet and simulation constants
known.gloss: A Turing machine's states and finite alphabet can encode several tracks or extra marks, and fixed changes of this kind change running time only by a constant factor.
